agent: <agent-name, matching your file name and your folder>
stage: <the stage number of the plan entry this answers, as a number. The first handoff you write in a run is handoff.json. A later plan entry writes handoff-stage<N>.json. A repeat pass at the same stage, such as a fix round or a re-review, writes handoff-stage<N>-round<R>.json. The orchestrator's run-open handoff.json uses 0.>
status: <passed, blocked, rejected or escalated. Nothing else.>
finished: <ISO 8601 UTC, from the shell, at hand-off>
consumed: <every path you actually read. Listing one you did not read falsifies the record.>
produced: <every path you wrote. Each must exist on disk and be non-empty.>

gates.name: <only a gate you own, by its name in run.json gates[]. Self-checks go in review.md, never here. Delete this entry if you own no gate.>
gates.evidence: <the path that proves the result. A pass with no evidence path is unresolved.>

blockers.what: <what is wrong or missing, with the round number on a rejection. A missing tool is a blocker, never faked: name the tool and the error.>

missing_inputs: <a promised input that never arrived and that you worked around, or a PROJECT.md section that lacks a fact you needed, named as 'PROJECT.md § <section>: <the missing fact>'>
machinery_findings: <an agent file, skill, template or script that was ambiguous or wrong, with the file named>

decisions_for_product_lead.question: <the decision, stated as a choice>
decisions_for_product_lead.recommendation: <your recommendation, with the reason. Never a bare question.>

next: <the agent-name that should run next on a pass, 'orchestrator' on a rejected, blocked or escalated handoff (blockers[].needs names who must act), 'product-lead', or null at run closure>
